text: It is the tears of the earth that keep her smiles in bloom.
note: sorrow and joy bound together; grief that nourishes

text: If you shed tears when you miss the sun, you also miss the stars.
note: dwelling on loss blinds you to what remains

text: Once we dreamt that we were strangers. We wake up to find that we were dear to each other.
Sorrow is hushed into peace in my heart like the evening among the silent trees.
Do not seat your love upon a precipice because it is high.
note: choosing love for status rather than safety

text: What you are you do not see, what you see is your shadow.
I cannot choose the best. The best chooses me.
note: letting go of the need to choose perfectly

text: They throw their shadows before them who carry their lantern on their back.
note: living by the past casts shadows ahead

text: That I exist is a perpetual surprise which is life.
Rest belongs to the work as the eyelids to the eyes.
note: rest as part of good work

text: Man is a born child, his power is the power of growth.
O Beauty, find thyself in love, not in the flattery of thy mirror.
Life finds its wealth by the claims of the world, and its worth by the claims of love.
note: worth found in love, not worldly demands

text: The dry river-bed finds no thanks for its past.
The bird wishes it were a cloud. The cloud wishes it were a bird.
note: envy; wanting to be someone else

text: The waterfall sings, "I find my song, when I find my freedom."
note: freedom as the source of true expression

text: Do not blame your food because you have no appetite.
note: blaming circumstances for your own state

text: You smiled and talked to me of nothing and I felt that for this I had been waiting long.
note: quiet companionship one has longed for

text: He has made his weapons his gods. When his weapons win he is defeated himself.
note: trusting force; winning that defeats you

text: The stars are not afraid to appear like fireflies.
The mind, sharp but not broad, sticks at every point but does not move.
Man does not reveal himself in his history, he struggles up through it.
Like the meeting of the seagulls and the waves we meet and come near. The seagulls fly off, the waves roll away and we depart.
My day is done, and I am like a boat drawn on the beach, listening to the dance-music of the tide in the evening.
note: ageing; the close of a working life

text: Life is given to us, we earn it by giving it.
We come nearest to the great when we are great in humility.
The sparrow is sorry for the peacock at the burden of its tail.
note: burdens of status; pity for the proud

text: Never be afraid of the moments--thus sings the voice of the everlasting.
Take my wine in my own cup, friend. It loses its wreath of foam when poured into that of others.
note: being valued as yourself, not compared

text: Thank the flame for its light, but do not forget the lampholder standing in the shade with constancy of patience.
Tiny grass, your steps are small, but you possess the earth under your tread.
Wrong cannot afford defeat but Right can.
"I give my whole water in joy," sings the waterfall, "though little of it is enough for the thirsty."
The woodcutter's axe begged for its handle from the tree. The tree gave it.
note: betrayal; giving to those who harm

text: We read the world wrong and say that it deceives us.
note: blaming the world for our misreading

text: The grass seeks her crowd in the earth. The tree seeks his solitude of the sky.
Let life be beautiful like summer flowers and death like autumn leaves.
He who wants to do good knocks at the gate; he who loves finds the gate open.
The scabbard is content to be dull when it protects the keenness of the sword.
Power said to the world, "You are mine. The world kept it prisoner on her throne. Love said to the world, "I am thine." The world gave it the freedom of her house.
I think of other ages that floated upon the stream of life and love and death and are forgotten, and I feel the freedom of passing away.
note: peace about being forgotten and passing

text: Death's stamp gives value to the coin of life; making it possible to buy with life what is truly precious.
The cloud stood humbly in a corner of the sky. The morning crowned it with splendour.
The dust receives insult and in return offers her flowers.
Do not linger to gather flowers to keep them, but walk on, for flowers will keep themselves blooming all your way.
Do not insult your friend by lending him merits from your own pocket.
I cast my own shadow upon my path, because I have a lamp that has not been lighted.
note: your own unlit potential blocks you

text: Man goes into the noisy crowd to drown his own clamour of silence.
The road is lonely in its crowd for it is not loved.
I carry in my world that flourishes the worlds that have failed.
note: carrying past failures within present success

text: Not hammerstrokes, but dance of the water sings the pebbles into perfection.
Bees sip honey from flowers and hum their thanks when they leave. The gaudy butterfly is sure that the flowers owe thanks to him.
To be outspoken is easy when you do not wait to speak the complete truth.
note: bluntness that is not full honesty

text: If you shut your door to all errors truth will be shut out.
note: fear of mistakes shuts out truth

text: The roots below the earth claim no rewards for making the branches fruitful.
Time is the wealth of change, but the clock in its parody makes it mere change and no wealth.
note: time well used versus merely passing

text: When I travelled to here and to there, I was tired of thee, O Road, but now when thou leadest me to everywhere I am wedded to thee in love.
Let me think that there is one among those stars that guides my life through the dark unknown.
note: hope for guidance through the unknown

text: One sad voice has its nest among the ruins of the years. It sings to me in the night,--"I loved you."
I have my stars in the sky, But oh for my little lamp unlit in my house.
note: neglecting what is close to home

text: The dust of the dead words clings to thee. Wash thy soul with silence.
note: silence to heal after empty words

text: Gaps are left in life through which comes the sad music of death.
The world has opened its heart of light in the morning. Come out, my heart, with thy love to meet it.
note: meeting a new day with love

text: God's great power is in the gentle breeze, not in the storm.
"Who is there to take up my duties?" asked the setting sun. "I shall do what I can, my Master," said the earthen lamp.
By plucking her petals you do not gather the beauty of the flower.
The Great walks with the Small without fear. The Middling keeps aloof.
When we rejoice in our fulness, then we can part with our fruits with joy.
note: giving from a sense of fullness

text: Love! when you come with the burning lamp of pain in your hand, I can see your face and know you as bliss.
The world has kissed my soul with its pain, asking for its return in songs.
Either you have work or you have not. When you have to say, "Let us do something," then begins mischief.
"Who drives me forward like fate?" "The Myself striding on my back."
I spill water from my water jar as I walk on my way, Very little remains for my home.
note: giving away so much little is left for home

text: The water in a vessel is sparkling; the water in the sea is dark. The small truth has words that are clear; the great truth has great silence.
It is the little things that I leave behind for my loved ones,-- great things are for everyone.
note: small personal gifts to loved ones

text: My flower of the day dropped its petals forgotten. In the evening it ripens into a golden fruit of memory.
He who is too busy doing good finds no time to be good.
note: busy doing good versus being good

text: I am the autumn cloud, empty of rain, see my fulness in the field of ripened rice.
Darkness travels towards light, but blindness towards death.
note: ignorance that seeks versus refuses to see

text: Sit still my heart, do not raise your dust. Let the world find its way to you.
note: stillness; letting things come to you

text: The bow whispers to the arrow before it speeds forth--"Your freedom is mine."
note: parenting; letting go of someone you love

text: A mind all logic is like a knife all blade. It makes the hand bleed that uses it.
note: too much logic hurts the thinker

text: By touching you may kill, by keeping away you may possess.
The wasp thinks that the honey-hive of the neighbouring bees is too small. His neighbours ask him to build one still smaller.
note: envy and petty criticism of others

text: "I cannot keep your waves," says the bank to the river. "Let me keep your footprints in my heart."
Let me not put myself wrongly to my world and set it against me.
Praise shames me, for I secretly beg for it.
Let my doing nothing when I have nothing to do become untroubled in its depth of peace like the evening in the seashore when the water is silent.
Our desire lends the colours of the rainbow to the mere mists and vapours of life.
note: desire colouring how we see life

text: My sad thoughts tease me asking me their own names.
The service of the fruit is precious, the service of the flower is sweet, but let my service be the service of the leaves in its shade of humble devotion.
Men are cruel, but Man is kind.
The world does not leak because death is not a crack.
note: death does not diminish the world

text: Life has become richer by the love that has been lost.
Kicks only raise dust and not crops from the earth.
note: anger and force bring no good

text: Our names are the light that glows on the sea waves at night and then dies without leaving its signature.
Let him only see the thorns who has eyes to see the rose.
Set bird's wings with gold and it will never again soar in the sky.
In heart's perspective the distance looms large.
note: distance felt more in the heart

text: The moon has her light all over the sky, her dark spots to herself.
Do not say, "It is morning," and dismiss it with a name of yesterday. See it for the first time as a new-born child that has no name.
The raindrop whispered to the jasmine, "Keep me in your heart for ever." The jasmine sighed, "Alas," and dropped to the ground.
Timid thoughts, do not be afraid of me. I am a poet.
Thou hast led me through my crowded travels of the day to my evening's loneliness. I wait for its meaning through the stillness of the night.
note: loneliness at day's end; seeking meaning

text: This life is the crossing of a sea, where we meet in the same narrow ship. In death we reach the shore and go to our different worlds.
note: companionship in life, parting in death

text: The stream of truth flows through its channels of mistakes.
My heart is homesick to-day for the one sweet hour across the sea of time.
note: nostalgia, homesick for a past moment

text: Let not the sword-blade mock its handle for being blunt.
The real with its meaning read wrong and emphasis misplaced is the unreal.
Find your beauty, my heart, from the world's movement, like the boat that has the grace of the wind and the water.
I live in this little world of mine and am afraid to make it the least less. Lift me into thy world and let me have the freedom gladly to lose my all.
note: fear of loss; freedom of letting go

text: The false can never grow into truth by growing in power.
note: power does not make falsehood true

text: The little flower lies in the dust. It sought the path of the butterfly.
I have sung the songs of thy day. In the evening let me carry thy lamp through the stormy path.
I do not ask thee into the house. Come into my infinite loneliness, my Lover.
Death belongs to life as birth does. The walk is in the raising of the foot as in the laying of it down.
I have learnt the simple meaning of thy whispers in flowers and sunshine--teach me to know thy words in pain and death.
note: seeking meaning in pain and death

text: Through the sadness of all things I hear the crooning of the Eternal Mother.
I came to your shore as a stranger, I lived in your house as a guest, I leave your door as a friend, my earth.
note: a life well lived; leaving as a friend

text: Let my thoughts come to you, when I am gone, like the afterglow of sunset at the margin of starry silence.
The day of work is done. Hide my face in your arms, Mother. Let me dream.
note: rest after work; need for comfort

text: The lamp of meeting burns long; it goes out in a moment at the parting.
note: parting and how fast it comes

text: One word keep for me in thy silence, O World, when I am dead, "I have loved."
note: wanting to be remembered as loving

text: We live in this world when we love it.
Let the dead have the immortality of fame, but the living the immortality of love.
I shall die again and again to know that life is inexhaustible.
While I was passing with the crowd in the road I saw thy smile from the balcony and I sang and forgot all noise.
note: love lifting one above the crowd

text: Love is life in its fulness like the cup with its wine.
Love's pain sang round my life like the unplumbed sea, and love's joy sang like birds in its flowering groves.
note: the pain and joy of love

text: Put out the lamp when thou wishest. I shall know thy darkness and shall love it.
When I stand before thee at the day's end thou shalt see my scars and know that I had my wounds and also my healing.
Clouds come floating into my life from other days no longer to shed rain or usher storm but to give colour to my sunset sky.
Truth raises against itself the storm that scatters its seeds broadcast.
The storm of the last night has crowned this morning with golden peace.
Blessed is he whose fame does not outshine his truth.
The world loved man when he smiled. The world became afraid of him when he laughed.
Thy sunshine smiles upon the winter days of my heart, never doubting of its spring flowers.
Thou crossest desert lands of barren years to reach the moment of fulfilment.

Cheerless is the day, the light under frowning clouds is like a punished child with traces of tears on its pale cheeks, and the cry of the wind is like the cry of a wounded world. But I know I am travelling to meet my Friend.
note: gloomy day, hope of meeting a friend

text: That love can ever lose is a fact that we cannot accept as truth.
note: refusing to believe love can be lost

text: We shall know some day that death can never rob us of that which our soul has gained, for her gains are one with herself.
note: death cannot take what the soul has gained

text: God comes to me in the dusk of my evening with the flowers from my past kept fresh in his basket.
note: past joys kept fresh in later life

text: Let me live truly, my Lord, so that death to me become true.
Man's history is waiting in patience for the triumph of the insulted man.
note: patience for justice for the wronged

text: I have scaled the peak and found no shelter in fame's bleak and barren height. Lead me, my Guide, before the light fades, into the valley of quiet where life's harvest mellows into golden wisdom.
note: emptiness of fame; seeking quiet wisdom

text: I have suffered and despaired and known death and I am glad that I am in this great world.
There are tracts in my life that are bare and silent. They are the open spaces where my busy days had their light and air.
Release me from my unfulfilled past clinging to me from behind making death difficult.
note: letting go of an unfulfilled past

text: Let this be my last word, that I trust in thy love.
